real_lan_discovery.observations: Replies come from port 20002. They carry BOTH encrypt_info (decrypted OK: full device_id, http_port 443, connect_ssid, ...) and a top-level device_id = UPPERCASE md5(deviceId); md5(decrypted id) equals the lowercased top-level value. Also present: sv 1, protocol_version 1, tpap {pake:[2], tls:1, noc:1, port:443}, mgt_encrypt_schm {is_support_https:true}.

decisions: TLS: the real cloud (n-wap.i.tplinkcloud.com, n-wap-gw.tplinkcloud.com) uses TP-Link private CAs ('TP-Link Cloud Server CA' -> 'TP-Link Cloud Root CA'); system-store validation FAILS. The two root PEMs from the APK (jadx m7/u.java) are embedded in core/cloud/_trust.py and added on top of the default store (make_ssl_context). A handshake-only check (no API call, no credentials) succeeded with them for both hosts.
Region: getAccountStatusAndUrl -> appServerUrlV2; login there; -20212 (result.appServerUrlV2) -> one retry at that URL. AccountInfo.region_url = regional URL.

Errors: envelope errorCode (int) and result.errorCode (string) are both checked. CloudAuthError for -20004/-20200/-20202/-20600/-20601/-20602/-20607/-20615/-20661/-20676/-20681/-20697/-20708 with user-facing messages (locked minutes / remaining attempts); -20677 -> CloudMfaRequired(process_id, mfa_types); others CloudError(code). Network/TLS/timeouts -> TapoConnectionError. Non-JSON -> CloudError('malformed' or HTTP status).

MFA: request_mfa_code 1 -> getPushVC4TerminalMFA (the app sends a push; the contract note said push needs no send, sending it is what the phone app does), 2 email, 4 SMS, 3 TOTP no-op; complete_mfa uses checkMFACodeAndLogin with terminalBindEnabled true. MFA methods without a pending login raise CloudError.
Token expiry: -20651 -> captchaLogin with stored email+password once, then the page is retried; -20652/-20675 -> one full login. A failing re-login raises (no loop).

Device list: body deviceTypeList [SMART.IPCAMERA, SMART.TAPODOORBELL, SMART.TAPOHUB] like the app, limit 20, index += 20 until totalNum; client keeps only SMART.IPCAMERA and SMART.TAPODOORBELL; dedupe by deviceId; mac normalised AA-BB-..; online = status != 0.
Alias: decode_alias() decodes only canonical padded Base64 that yields printable UTF-8 (e.g. 'Cam1', 'Home' stay raw); empty alias falls back to deviceName then model.

Login strings: platform 'Android 14' (mimics the app; server validation for desktop strings unknown), terminalName 'Tapo Desktop (Windows PC)' (shown in the account's trusted devices), ospf '<OS> <release>', netType 'wifi', locale from the OS (fallback en_US).

Secrets: password/token live in name-mangled private attributes; repr/str show only base_url, signed_in, mfa_pending; logs contain path, error code and region host only; the query string (with token) is never logged.

TDP: discover() sends attempts x probes (default 3, 0.3 s apart) to every target, listens until timeout, dedupes by normalised MAC, sorts by IP, never raises for network errors (WSAECONNRESET ignored). Default targets add port 20004 (spec: camera scans also use it) and each up interface's directed broadcast via iphlpapi GetIpAddrTable (fallback /24). One RSA-2048 key pair per process, like the app. parse_response gained an optional keyword serial=None (additive) to enforce the request serial; it tolerates concatenated packets and returns the first. Undecryptable encrypt_info falls back to the top-level md5 device_id.
Matcher: md5(deviceId) first, then MAC among LAN devices not yet assigned; each LAN device is used once; normalise_mac returns '' for invalid input so junk never matches.

Fixtures: mock_cloud / mock_tdp are started default instances (mutable attributes); mock_cloud_factory / mock_tdp_factory build custom ones. phase2_fixtures exports DEFAULT_EMAIL, DEFAULT_PASSWORD, DEFAULT_CLOUD_DEVICES (2 cameras + 1 plug), DEFAULT_TDP_DEVICES (the 2 cameras at 127.0.0.1) and tdp_device_for() so other lanes can test sign-in -> list -> discover -> match end to end. MockTapoCloud verifies Content-MD5 + X-Authorization independently (HTTP 401 errorCode -1 otherwise) and emulates region redirect, MFA with terminal binding, locked accounts, token expiry and paging.
